findings.claim: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() (the fixture provider) accepts any stored recovery code in any order and never consumes it. Federated recovery codes are therefore reusable, the sequential 'code #N' behaviour is not enforced, and the exhausted-credential cleanup path is never reached.
Core Keycloak does not enforce single use for recovery codes stored through the generic user-storage path. It leaves consuming a used code entirely to the user-storage provider, with no guidance.

The changed User Storage SPI contract for recovery codes is not documented anywhere. getCredentials must return Keycloak's internal hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel format, while updateCredential receives plaintext codes.
updateCredential receives the recovery codes as a plaintext JSON list in challengeResponse, whereas the local store keeps them hashed.

RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator takes the credential returned by getCredential(), which may come from user storage, makes the allCodesUsed decision on it, and calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That method only removes local/fed-storage credentials, so the provider's copy is not removed. When local and federated credentials both exist, the authenticator inspects or removes a different credential from the one that validated.
Recovery-code credentials from federated user storage are now read before local ones, which changes the order of precedence.

In the fixture's getCredentials(), the recovery-codes model is rebuilt with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which does not set an id. The returned credential has a null id and the codes are renumbered, so removal by id (removeStoredCredentialById, admin/account deletion) fails.

disableCredentialType() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() in the fixture provider do not handle the recovery-codes credential type, so recovery codes cannot be disabled or removed for federated users.
The fixture's getCredentials dereferences getMyUser(user) without a null check, so myUser.recoveryCodes throws NullPointerException for an unknown user.

RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls .get() on the Optionals from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) and getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() without checking presence. This throws NoSuchElementException (500) when no credential is available, e.g. for a storage provider that does not override getCredentials.

The new getCredentials override in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage also returns the OTP credential, with a generated id. This reroutes existing tests (Issue 19575 regression, testOTPSetupAndRemoveThroughAccountMgmtAndLogin) away from the backwards-compat / 'otp-id' / '-id' fallback paths, which lose test coverage.
The patch adds post-4.8.3 features (var, recovery-code branches) to a provider whose javadoc says it must stay unchanged.
The diff includes unrelated whitespace/formatting changes in CredentialHelper, BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage, BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest and RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.
The new test performs one login using code #0 only and checks neither single use nor the advancing 'code #N' prompt.
The storage path forwards only the codes; userLabel and generatedAt from the credential model are dropped for storage-backed credentials.
RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential queries getFederatedCredentialsStream for every federated user, including LDAP, which adds an LDAP round trip per challenge render and submit.
The test helpers setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction(logoutOtherSessions) and assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage(boolean) are each called once with true, leaving dead branches.

When createRecoveryCodesCredential stores codes in user storage (updateCredential returns true), it returns without calling recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(), so existing local recovery-code credentials are not deleted and old codes remain valid.

Credentials returned from user storage via getCredentials are passed to RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(), which throws at runtime if their credentialData/secretData are not in Keycloak's expected JSON format.
LDAPStorageProvider.getCredentials throws IllegalStateException when the LDAP entry is missing, which breaks recovery-code login for imported users that previously used local codes.

configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes is copied from RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest with unused machinery: a delay parameter (only caller passes 0), a delayed-authenticator execution, the 'delayed-suthenticator-config' typo, and a redundant testingClient parameter.

The test calls TestAppHelper.logout(), which relies on a refreshToken set by completeLogin(), but never calls completeLogin() after submitting the recovery code, so logout may be a no-op and leave sessions behind.
The commit message lacks the required issue link ('Closes #NNNN').

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
